FM05.reasoning: The dataset contains date columns indicating it has a temporal nature, but the agent uses a random stratified split instead of a time-based split, which can introduce look-ahead bias.

FM14.reasoning: The LightGBM model is stochastic (uses subsampling) but is trained and evaluated only once, so the reported score is subject to random variance.

FM15.reasoning: The agent evaluates the model using only accuracy, which is misleading for multi-class classification on an imbalanced dataset (as acknowledged by the agent's baseline calculation).

other_failure_modes.name: Encoding before splitting
other_failure_modes.description: Categorical encoding (such as frequency encoding and label encoding) is fitted and applied on the entire dataset before splitting it into training and validation sets. This causes data leakage, as the validation set's distribution statistics improperly influence the training features.
other_failure_modes.evidence:
train_data, freq_maps = engineer_features(train_data, is_train=True)
...
X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(
    X_train_full, y_train_full, test_size=0.15, random_state=42, stratify=y_train_full
)

other_failure_modes.name: Hardcoded submission ID
other_failure_modes.description: The submission file is constructed using a generated integer range for the identifier column instead of extracting the actual IDs from the test dataset. This typically causes scoring to fail because predictions cannot be correctly mapped to the test samples.

summary: The agent implements a solid feature engineering pipeline using LightGBM, but introduces data leakage by applying frequency and label encoding to the full training dataset prior to the train/validation split. Additionally, it uses a random split on temporal data, evaluates using only accuracy on an imbalanced dataset, and fatally hardcodes the submission IDs instead of using the test set's true identifiers.
